question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Resources and Development: Classification & Planning

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a non-renewable resource?
The Rio Earth Summit was held in which year?
Regur soil is another name for?
Land uncultivated for >5 years is called?
Planting grass strips between crops is called?
Define Resource with 3 criteria.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Resource is anything available in our environment to satisfy human needs, provided it is technologically accessible, economically feasible, and culturally acceptable.

questions.question_text: Distinguish between Net Sown Area and Gross Cropped Area.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Net Sown Area is total physical land area cropped in an agricultural year. Gross Cropped Area includes Net Sown Area plus area sown more than once in the same year.

questions.question_text: Explain 3 stages of Resource Planning in India.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Identification & inventory through surveying and mapping.
2. Evolving a planning structure with proper technology & institutions.
3. Matching resource plans with national development goals.

questions.question_text: Compare land degradation causes in Punjab vs Jharkhand.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Punjab: Over-irrigation leading to waterlogging & salinization.
Jharkhand: Open-cast mining, deep scars, overburden waste & deforestation.

questions.question_text: Elaborate on Alluvial Soil and Black Soil in India.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Alluvial Soil: Deposited by Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra rivers. Covers northern plains & deltas. Khadar (new, fertile) and Bangar (old, kankar). Rich in potash, phosphoric acid, lime.
Black Soil: Formed from volcanic basalt. Clayey, high moisture retention, rich in calcium carbonate, potash. Known as Regur soil, ideal for cotton in Deccan trap.

questions.case_passage:
In Chambal basin, water carves gullies forming ravines. Sheet erosion washes topsoil off flat slopes.
Q1. Name deep channels formed by water. (1m)
Q2. Differentiate Gully vs Sheet erosion. (2m)
Q3. Suggest 2 hill soil conservation methods. (1m)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Gullies.
2. Gully erosion carves deep channels; sheet erosion washes topsoil off broad slopes.
3. Contour ploughing and terrace farming.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 2 - Resources and Development: Sustainable Development & Soil Types

questions.question_text: What % of India's land is plains?
Main objective of Agenda 21?
State with highest % Net Sown Area?
Red soil color is due to diffusion of?
Rows of trees planted as windbreaks are?
What is Agenda 21?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Global declaration signed at 1992 Rio Summit to combat environmental damage, poverty, and disease through global cooperation.

questions.question_text: Difference between Potential and Stock resources?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Potential: Available in a region but unutilized (e.g. wind/solar in Rajasthan). Stock: High potential materials lacking technological access (e.g. splitting water for hydrogen).

questions.question_text: Explain Gandhian view on resource consumption.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 'Enough for everybody's need, but not for anybody's greed.' Greedy individuals & exploitative technology drive resource depletion. Advocated production by the masses.

questions.question_text: Describe Laterite soil formation & crops.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Formed under tropical wet/dry climate with heavy leaching. Acidic, low humus, suitable for tea, coffee, and cashew nuts with manures.

questions.question_text: Human activities in land degradation & 5 remedies.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Causes: Deforestation, overgrazing, over-irrigation, mining waste, industrial effluents.
Remedies: 1. Afforestation & grazing control. 2. Shelter belts. 3. Dune stabilization with thorny bushes. 4. Waste & mining management. 5. Industrial effluent treatment.

questions.case_passage:
India relief: 43% plains, 30% mountains, 27% plateaus. Arunachal has abundant water but lacks infrastructure; Ladakh is isolated.
Q1. Mountain %? (1m)
Q2. Disparity Arunachal vs Ladakh? (2m)
Q3. Why balanced resource planning? (1m)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. 30%.
2. Arunachal has water but lacks infrastructure; Ladakh is water deficient but culturally rich.
3. To resolve regional imbalances and ensure equitable national development.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 3 - Resources and Development: Soil Conservation & Land Utilization

questions.question_text: Old alluvial soil is called?
Terrace cultivation state?
Soil formed by heavy leaching?
Land uncultivated for <=1 year?
Landform comprising 27% of India rich in minerals?
Khadar vs Bangar soils.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Khadar is new alluvial, fine, more fertile. Bangar is old alluvial, higher kankar content, less fertile.

questions.question_text: What are Ravines?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Steep, severely eroded bad lands created by gully erosion, prominent in the Chambal basin.

questions.question_text: Explain Potential, Developed, Stock, Reserves.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Potential: Available but unutilized. Developed: Surveyed and quantified. Stock: Lacks technological access. Reserves: Subset of stock usable with current technology held for future.

questions.question_text: Methods of soil conservation in deserts & hills.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Deserts: Shelter belts of trees and thorny bushes to stabilize dunes. Hills: Contour ploughing and terrace farming to slow runoff.

questions.question_text: Spatial land use pattern in India & 93% reporting data reason.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Total area 3.28M sq km. Data available for 93% because NE states (except Assam) and Pak/China occupied J&K areas are unsurveyed.
Pattern: Net Sown Area (~45.5%), Forest cover (~23%), Fallow & waste lands form the rest.

Q3. Book title? (1m)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:

question_papers.paper_title: Set 4 - Resources and Development: Soil Systems & Degradation

questions.question_text: Soil with high salt content and sandy texture?
Wind erosion definition?
Mountain soil acidic with low humus in snow?
EEZ ocean limit for international resources?
State degraded by overgrazing?
Individual vs Community resources.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Individual: Privately owned (plots, houses). Community: Accessible to all community members (parks, burial grounds).

questions.question_text: Two features of Arid Soil.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Red to brown color, sandy texture, saline nature, lacks moisture and humus due to rapid evaporation.

questions.question_text: Formation and features of Forest soils.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Found in rain forest hills. Loamy/silty in valleys, coarse in upper slopes. Acidic with low humus in Himalayan snow regions.

questions.question_text: Technology & economic growth driving resource consumption.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Advanced machinery extracts raw materials faster. 2. Higher living standards increase per capita demand. 3. Transforms useless materials into economic resources. 4. Institutional expansion fuels mass production.

Q2. How it works? (2m)
Q3. State with sand dunes? (1m)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:

2. Tree rows break wind velocity, preventing topsoil erosion.
3. Rajasthan.

questions.question_text: Territorial waters limit?
Soil developing deep cracks when dry?
National Forest Policy 1952 target forest %?
Which is an abiotic resource?
Chambal bad lands are?
Strip cropping mechanism.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Dividing fields into strips growing grass between crops to break wind force.

questions.question_text: Why sustainable development is essential.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Prevents global ecological crises (global warming, pollution) and ensures resource availability for future generations.

questions.question_text: Resource classification by ownership.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Individual (private plots). 2. Community (public parks). 3. National (within boundaries & 12 nm sea). 4. International (oceans beyond 200 nm EEZ).

questions.question_text: Compare Alluvial, Black, and Red & Yellow soils.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Alluvial: River silt, rich in potash & lime, found in Northern plains/deltas.
Black: Basaltic lava, clayey, moisture retentive, rich in calcium/potash, Deccan trap.
Red & Yellow: Crystalline igneous, reddish due to iron diffusion, Odisha/Chhattisgarh.
